## Coordinator instructions

1. Fetch the exact merged docs commit above, read current repository instructions and inspect the actual implementation revision. Preserve unrelated user edits. Use the single order below; read the linked issue for its bounded output and exact tests rather than copying full bodies here.
2. Take the first unfinished applicable task whose inputs are genuinely unblocked. Retrieve and verify predecessor artifact/receipt locator, hash, scope, candidate/profile, authorized actor and non-superseded status. A closed issue, planned path or schema-valid receipt is not passing evidence. Name concrete missing outputs/authority; unrelated ready work may proceed without waiving that blocker.
3. Apply hard, conditional and alternative predicates precisely. #1003 is conditional for #1004 annual_offline_request and #1015/#1017 selected annual_offline_profile; Local/nonannual requests and ordinary parity/restore remain independent. H is cross-cutting. Decline/defer never equals qualification or automatic scope removal. Expansions retain main-release and exact access/reference/physical/field gates. Every source/reference human owner owns its finite resource disposition; #804 stays at 409 and is not a universal campaign prerequisite.
4. Produce bounded progress receipts: task and immutable revision, verified inputs, changed paths, commands with pass/fail/blocked/not-run results, output locator/hash, remaining blocker and next handoff. Preserve task/ID lineage, original numeric gates, existing source/legacy rights and independent human decisions. Give no effort estimates.
5. Reports E/F/I/J were supplied; A–D/G/H remain missing. Planning/publication checks are not product implementation, real hardware/field qualification or human AT observation. Included optional features need enabled and absent/disabled evidence. Existing releases do not prove this roadmap shipped. Scoped external actions need their own authority; #799 remains the human main-release gate.

# Pillar creator diagnostics architecture and code quality plan

Prepared 10 October 2026 for the approved creator, local-model, optional-browser and managed-continuity work. Updated 10 October 2026 for the owner’s optional-model decision and subsequent approval of a one-time Pillar Local license after a full trial. These decisions supersede earlier bundled-by-default model packaging and permanent full-Free product language. Exact commercial release terms remain subject to the existing human approval gates.

## Purpose and decision

Build the new experience around one authoritative deterministic evidence engine. The default client stays lightweight and model-free: under any surviving valid trial, purchased Local, subscription-derived or retained legacy grant, core collection, deterministic findings, qualified answers, history and export remain useful without model assets or inference. After one grant expires, new diagnostic use continues if another valid grant covers it; retained reports/exports remain accessible. Users may separately download an approved signed local model pack and enable it to propose read-only questions and explain verified answers. The browser companion supplies only explicitly enabled playback observations and does not require the model. Hosted services retain and deliver only approved compact projections. Every presentation must preserve the same evidence strength, uncertainty and expiry.

This is an implementation architecture and review plan, not an implementation result or permission to install software, collect new data, activate an offer, migrate a live database or release a product. The existing issue dependency order remains authoritative. This revision records the owner-approved Local licensing direction below; it does not activate an offer or invent further prices, quotas, renewal rules or retention promises.

### Evidence reviewed

- GitHub default branch `main`, commit [`bd4d32c5b8024102363204596a7557df32c412b8`](https://github.com/Pillar-Interactive/pillar/commit/bd4d32c5b8024102363204596a7557df32c412b8), was inspected through the read-only GitHub connector. - The frozen creator/managed-continuity supplements form the preceding 331-task baseline. The current Local-licensing amendment adds one bounded runtime feature-admission task, producing 332 tasks across 28 milestones. These plans supply contracts and acceptance gates, not proof the components exist.
- The original source plans on the owner's Mac remain uncommitted user-owned inputs. They were not overwritten. The current remote tree has no `docs/plans/storage-journey*` files; reconcile those source plans in the transition inventory before committing a replacement architecture document.

## Existing architecture verified in code

| Repository | pnpm 10.13.1 workspace over `apps/*` and `packages/*`; Go agent, observer and CLI are separate modules. Web declares Next.js 16.3.6 and React 19.2.8. Agent declares Go 1.25.0 language level and go1.26.8 toolchain. | Do not create a second dependency system or infer a desktop framework from the existing web app. |
| Go edge collection | `internal/collector` runs ordered typed stages against a shared payload environment, records each stage's error and continues. It intentionally avoids a generic stringly typed metric bag. | Preserve typed adapters and explicit partial collection. New macOS collectors need their own qualified source profile; this Linux/NAS-oriented path is not proof of macOS support. |
| Observer and agent delivery | Observer windowing has monotonic durations, clock-change and backlog quality handling. The agent has a bounded durable spool and a v2 queue keyed by session and sequence, with per-window acknowledgments. | Reuse durability and protocol lessons; do not call the existing transport the new canonical summary store or assume it meets the future managed-delivery profile. |
| Hosted entry point | The Next.js heartbeat route authenticates a hashed node key, applies DB-backed rate limiting, limits actual compressed and decompressed bytes, calls ingest and returns `commands: []`. The agent ignores executable response commands. | Keep observe-only behavior. New projection intake must preserve authentication, body limits and explicit response semantics. |
| Current factual computation | `packages/pipeline` is a pure TypeScript normalize → evaluate → reconcile path. `packages/diagnostics` evaluates deterministic rules; the current ingest and simulator share the pipeline. | This is the existing authority. The proposed unprivileged Go engine is a migration, not an already shipped package. |
| Contracts | `packages/schema` owns Zod wire/domain schemas. `schema:generate` emits telemetry and observer IPC JSON Schema. ## Proposed component architecture

The names below are logical ownership boundaries, not invented existing folders. The transition inventory and native packaging decision must bind them to exact files before implementation.

```text
Already enabled native sources       Explicitly selected browser tab or site
             |                         optional extension observer
             |                               |
       native adapters                authenticated native bridge
             |                               |
             +------ source and capability validation ------+
                                    |
                     typed sanitizer and scoped identities
                                    |
                    bounded normalized observation pipeline
                             /               \
                   current snapshot      bounded local history
                             \               /
                      deterministic canonical Go engine
                                    |
                  versioned answers and evidence references
                      /             |                  \
                 native UI    read-only local API     approved sync projection
                                    |                  |
                           investigation controller   durable bounded queue
                                    |                  |
                        optional model helper         hosted authenticated ingest
                        proposes calls and wording     |
                                                    Neon summaries and control data
                                                       |
                                         canonical history and maintenance jobs
                                                       |
                                          episodes and periodic digest record
                                                       |
                                         consented notification outbox

Optional explicitly shared diagnostic bundles use the existing export path
and a separately approved object-storage profile, never a raw-stream warehouse.
```

### Native observation and local history

The native source profile owns exactly which CPU, memory/swap, disk, network and permitted GPU/thermal facts are available with ordinary permissions. An unsupported API or denied permission yields a capability state. It does not trigger a privileged fallback or fabricated measurement. Process context is scoped and bounded; process command lines and project content are excluded.

The sanitizer is the only constructor of persistable/exportable observation values. Sanitization happens before queues, local files, logs, crash diagnostics and hosted serialization. Keep raw adapter inputs short-lived. Preserve units, counts, provenance and explicit missing values while rejecting unknown sensitive fields.

The local recorder accepts only normalized summaries, schema/source/configuration epochs, quality and expiry. Its interface must support append, pinned snapshot read, available-range lookup, bounded eviction and recovery. A single logical writer serializes durable state changes; readers use immutable snapshots so collection can continue during pagination. The actual store/backend remains an explicit package decision, not a silently adopted new dependency.

Local history retains the adopted 30-day default, configurable up to 90 days within the existing 1 GiB observation/history bound and stricter field/source limits. Model files do not fit inside or expand that cap. Optional raw capture retains its separately governed existing limits and is not enabled by an investigation or browser session.

### One authoritative evidence engine

The planned ordinary-user Go engine owns quantity/clock compatibility, coverage propagation, graph/finding algorithms, question dispatch and immutable answer snapshots. Inputs include normalized observations, versions, selected scope/window and explicit time; the engine must not fetch a network source, read arbitrary files or consult a model while evaluating a question.

The TypeScript UI, hosted consumers and model interpreter consume serialized canonical results. During migration the current TypeScript authority stays operational. Port one rule family at a time under #921/#976, compare factual outputs against independent fixtures, resolve every discrepancy explicitly, then cut over only that family. Do not leave two independently evolving authorities, and do not retire useful existing health, capacity or incident behavior merely because a new engine starts.

The implementation decision must explain how hosted history executes the same canonical semantics: which bounded service/library/process owns evaluation and which serialized contract the Next.js routes consume. Selecting a Go runtime placement is required before hosted cutover; this document does not pretend Next.js can import a Go module directly.

### Local investigation controller and model helper

The controller is the sole caller of an installed, explicitly enabled model helper and the sole executor of its proposed tools. It owns the state machine `requested → scoped → running → completed`, with explicit `partial`, `cancelled`, `expired` and `unavailable` outcomes. Every job pins question, resource/source scope, snapshot, grant revision and resource-policy version.

The helper returns a schema-constrained proposal or explanation. The controller separately validates catalog membership, argument types, scope, evidence IDs, current authorization and remaining budget before each call and before presenting the result. Valid JSON is not evidence of a correct conclusion. Missing, stale, contradictory or unsupported evidence cannot be promoted to an asserted fact by model prose.

Run inference only after the user enables an installed, qualified pack, in a restricted local helper process with no arbitrary filesystem, network, shell or device-control access. An OS-enforced sandbox/resource policy should back the application checks; if a supported platform cannot enforce a promised bound, its qualification must record that limitation. Use one cancellable lifecycle for load, run, idle, unload, preempt and recovery. Start conservatively with one active generation and a bounded pending queue; the approved measured profile, not model output, sets final numeric limits.

The fixed read-only tools are the existing planned capability discovery, selected scope/window, canonical questions and allowed evidence retrieval. Reuse the authenticated local API and MCP catalog rather than create a second unauthenticated inference server. A model may suggest that the user enable a source; it cannot request a grant, activate capture, change settings, run a speed/DNS/TLS probe or generate a workload.

Prompts and sanitized context remain bounded local memory by default. Do not put transcripts in observation storage, sync, exports or crash reports. Not-installed or disabled means no resident model, no warm inference process and no inference work. Disabling cancels active/pending model work and unloads the helper; installation alone does not enable it. Users can remove the optional pack without removing local history or core collection. Corrupt, missing, incompatible or preempted inference returns useful deterministic answers with the explicit model status. There is no automatic hosted fallback or automatic pack reinstallation.

**Candidate research is separate from the architecture.** The current recommendation is to evaluate Qwen3.5-4B Q4_K_M GGUF with embedded llama.cpp first and Gemma 4 E2B as runner-up. Neither has been benchmarked for Pillar. #1105 and the exact human receipt in #1106 adopt the model, conversion provenance, runtime, hardware profile and resource limits. The verified owner development machine is an M4 MacBook Air with 24 GiB RAM; that does not establish the minimum customer configuration. The architecture permits replacing the evaluated candidate without changing the factual engine or tool authority. Qualification defines which clients can enable the optional pack; a lightweight client may remain fully model-free.

### Optional browser playback source

Chrome-first extension code observes only a user-selected tab/site. Browser and native-host identities are bound to a revocable session on the existing Mac endpoint; the tab creates no new billable endpoint. The bridge authenticates the allowed extension and native host, validates bounded message types and size before allocation, and rejects replay, stale sessions and unexpected origins/extension identities. The selected implementation must document its actual browser Native Messaging framing and process lifetime.

Allowed observations are exposed playback state, buffering intervals, dropped-frame counters and dimensions. Keep only approved coarse service identity and ephemeral local correlation IDs. No titles, full/page/media URLs, cookies, tokens, DOM text, page/media content or browsing history enter telemetry. A protected, missing or cross-origin signal is a typed limitation.

Browser input is untrusted even when the extension is installed. Its messages cannot carry executable instructions or become model authority. Navigation, tab closure, browser restart and revoke terminate or rotate the scoped session without linking unrelated browsing. Native facts remain useful without the extension.

Chrome Netflix/Plex claims require the actual permitted service/profile packet and qualification. Edge and Brave require their own evidence; Safari/Firefox are outside the initial companion. Apple TV remains the separate post-main-release source/reference/adapter/qualification expansion.

### Hosted continuity and optional bundles

An explicit sharing projection selects fields, sources, scope and expiry from sanitized local records before durable enqueue. Neon stores those compact canonical summaries, necessary account/control-plane data, versions, receipts and delivery metadata. It does not store raw browser/process/media streams, prompts, inference context or weights.

Optional diagnostic bundles use the approved archive/export contract. If a selected delivery profile uses object storage, give each object the same tenant/grant/expiry/delete checks and verified checksum as its manifest. A database pointer is not permission to download; authorize retrieval at use time. Keep this optional path out of ordinary summary ingest and out of any customer-media-backup claim.

The periodic digest is one deterministic computation over approved retained evidence: recurring supported interruptions, observed configuration changes and valid comparable-window outcomes. It reuses history, configuration epochs, comparison, episode and job components. It is not a hosted LLM or a second comparison engine. The delivery component owns explicit opt-in, bounded cadence, recipients and the existing outbox. The separate cloud subscription supplies approved off-device retention/access/delivery convenience within adopted terms. The Local entitlement governs new local diagnostic use after the trial, through purchased rights or temporary subscription-covered access. Neither payment path strengthens factual certainty, rewrites retained findings or certifies health when new observations are unavailable.

## Trust boundaries and privacy enforcement

1. **OS and source boundary:** source availability and user permission are inputs, never implied by installation. Collect only declared passive observations. A failure in one adapter cannot silently enable another.
2. **Browser boundary:** page-derived data and external strings remain untrusted; sanitize before persistence or model exposure. The bridge accepts a finite protocol, not commands.
3. **Model boundary:** the controller, grant store and engine outrank all model output. The helper cannot mint references, authorize tools, change expiry or write findings as measured facts.
4. **Local client boundary:** stdio or approved loopback/IPC transport must authenticate clients and constrain scope. Separately check all surviving valid feature grants for new private-engine diagnostic operations; reading retained reports and exporting allowed retained data stay available after trial expiry. Network-disabled licensed operation is required. Do not open a remote listener as an incidental packaging choice.
5. **Sync boundary:** explicit sharing and field allowlisting precede queue writes. Revalidate consent, scope and expiry immediately before transmission; the server independently revalidates tenant/resource ownership.
6. **Hosted and notification boundary:** cached queries, export links, jobs and sends recheck revocation and entitlement. A previously authorized queue entry is not continuing permission. Once an external provider has accepted a message, do not claim it can be unsent by revoking a local grant.
7. **Update boundary:** signed asset verification is independent of model reasoning and network availability. A model cannot select or download arbitrary replacements.

Use one dependency-aware expiry policy across source records, summaries, answers, digests, caches and controlled bundles. A derived claim expires no later than its shortest contributing evidence. Recomputing, importing, restoring or re-delivering a record never resets its observation age. Admin-audit retention must not smuggle expired observation behavior into a longer-lived class. Customer-owned exported copies have an explicit limit on what Pillar can later revoke.

Use structured, bounded logs containing component/version, stage, scoped opaque IDs, counts, timings, quality transitions and typed stop reasons. Never log raw prompt/context, paths, command lines, page/media identifiers, secrets or raw SQL/driver errors. Canary tests must cover exceptions, cancellation, overflow, retry, crash, backup and support export, not just successful serializers. Local inference memory can be released and excluded from application dumps; do not promise that an app controls every OS swap/crash artifact without platform evidence.

## Time coverage and factual semantics

- Use half-open observation/query periods with explicit UTC boundaries. Measure local elapsed durations using a monotonic clock; retain clock domain, epoch and alignment uncertainty for cross-source comparisons. Server receive time is not observation time.
- A counter requires a compatible previous sample, elapsed interval and reset/wrap handling. Reboot, PID reuse, source restart, configuration change or clock discontinuity begins a new comparable epoch as applicable.
- Distinguish `zero observed`, `unsupported`, `permission denied`, `not enabled`, `missing`, `lost`, `stale`, `expired` and `budget limited`. Empty history or an offline source cannot become a healthy zero.
- Keep one-minute summary resolution separate from transport batching. The approved 60–300-second bulk/urgent-lane contract remains controlling. A 5–15-minute batching experiment is not permission to change it.
- Preserve histogram layout, timing basis, population, counts and coverage. Never average percentiles into a claimed percentile; combine compatible distributions or return a limitation.
- A playback interruption coincident with memory, disk or network pressure supports correlation only. A causal claim requires that source/profile's qualified evidence. Missing protected playback counters cannot be inferred from throughput.
- Before/after comparisons require compatible scope, source/configuration/population epochs, exposure and denominator. Missing baseline or inadequate coverage yields qualified/inconclusive output. The digest consumes this existing comparator; it cannot tell a more confident story than the underlying answer.
- Hosted pages and digests show last observation, available period/resolution and gaps. A sleeping or offline Mac has historical observations, not live coverage.

## Concurrency backpressure and delivery

Collection, storage, queries, inference and sync have separate bounded work queues and cancellation paths. Inference never blocks source sampling or durable maintenance. Avoid a goroutine/promise per source event and unbounded `Promise.all` over tenant histories. Freeze buffers under short locks and perform slow I/O outside critical sections when the storage contract permits it. Inject clock and cancellation in tests rather than sleep through real TTLs.

The controller holds an investigation-wide budget across retries and pages. Nested calls cannot reset it. Cancellation, grant revocation, app shutdown, suspend/resume and pressure preemption release slots and invalidate pending work. Deadline-expired results are not delivered later under a refreshed grant. Snapshot cursors bind scope, authorization revision, snapshot/version and expiry so concurrent writes cannot create skipped, duplicated or unauthorized pages.

The local history writer and sync queue are separate ownership domains. A full sync queue cannot freeze local answers. Define admission, coalescing, drop/eviction order and visible gap accounting for each class before shipping. Keep urgent eligible incidents separate from ordinary summaries and periodic digests. Numeric caps and the durable acknowledgment boundary belong to #970; existing spool defaults are implementation facts, not proof of the new delivery guarantee.

For new sync records use stable tenant/producer/epoch/sequence identity plus canonical content hash. Repeated identical records are duplicates; the same identity with changed content is a conflict. Reordering must not regress the latest-state watermark or combine incompatible epochs. A lost response after commit is retried against the same identity. Reject/expire permanently invalid records; retry only classified transient failures with bounded backoff/jitter and fairness. A missing acknowledgment never implies durable acceptance.

The current observer path already demonstrates these distinctions: [queue](https://github.com/Pillar-Interactive/pillar/blob/bd4d32c5b8024102363204596a7557df32c412b8/apps/agent/internal/heartbeat/observer_queue.go), [spool](https://github.com/Pillar-Interactive/pillar/blob/bd4d32c5b8024102363204596a7557df32c412b8/apps/agent/internal/spool/spool.go), [transport](https://github.com/Pillar-Interactive/pillar/blob/bd4d32c5b8024102363204596a7557df32c412b8/apps/agent/internal/transport/client.go), [atomic hosted window ingest](https://github.com/Pillar-Interactive/pillar/blob/bd4d32c5b8024102363204596a7557df32c412b8/apps/web/src/lib/ingest/observerWindows.ts). Ordinary heartbeat writes are not all one global transaction and some sample inserts lack a per-heartbeat conflict clause; do not claim universal exactly-once ingestion from the observer guarantee alone.

Maintenance jobs use bounded leases, per-tenant/policy checkpoints, idempotent writes and explicit watermarks. A poisoned item cannot starve another tenant. Lease expiry and concurrent workers require a fence or equivalent conditional commit so an old worker cannot overwrite a newer result. Count deletion and repair work within the same budget.

Digest identity includes canonical scope, period, policy and evidence revision. Delivery identity is deliberately independent of digest revision: one logical delivery per tenant/schedule/recipient/channel/scope/period. Recompute an unsent payload under that identity; do not send another message merely because its evidence revision changed. After delivery, late evidence updates the in-app record without an automatic correction resend. Prevent duplicate active schedules for the same recipient/channel/scope and define timezone/DST, missed-period and rescheduling behavior. Reconcile uncertain provider acknowledgment instead of blind resend; do not promise exactly-once external delivery unless the selected provider's contract supports it.

## Resource and cost budgets

Enforce budgets before expensive allocation and again at boundary crossings. Each qualified profile records the hardware/OS/source estate, versions, measurement procedure, baseline and observed variability. No unmeasured profile becomes a customer minimum.

| Budget owner | Bound and measurement |
| --- | --- |
| Collection | Per-source cadence, rows/cardinality, CPU time, allocation/bytes, dropped observations, own disk/network I/O and dense-estate contention. |
| Local history | Existing 1 GiB observation/history cap plus adopted time/field limits; include indexes, journals and the accounting boundary explicitly. Measure eviction and restart peaks. |
| Query/controller | Window size, scanned rows, evidence bytes, pages, simultaneous jobs, call/retry count, elapsed time and cancellation delay. |
| Inference | Verify zero model residency/inference when absent or disabled. When enabled, measure loaded and peak RAM/VRAM, CPU/GPU use, context/output tokens, cold/warm latency, idle-unload and pressure-preemption behavior; foreground editing/export regression. |
| Optional model delivery | Separate finite model/runtime/cache/staging/rollback budgets for opted-in installations; total pack install/update peak free space; full/delta/resume/retry/removal bytes. Model-free installs incur no mandatory pack download or storage. |
| Sync/hosted | Batch bytes and compression, queue depth/age, peak rate, ten-minute store-outage summary survival and 24-hour retained-incident replay within the qualified profile. |
| Jobs/digests | Rows scanned, DB/query time, temporary and retained bytes, scheduling, retry/delivery count, per-tenant fairness and incremental support burden. |

Current transport limits are 1,900,000 uncompressed bytes on the agent and 2,000,000 actual compressed/decompressed bytes at the hosted route. These are verified existing safety limits, not a recommended payload allocation or a new pricing quota. Preserve or deliberately version them while the new projection is sized.

Measure Neon row/index/WAL/backup/maintenance/deletion/query costs and optional object-store operation/egress costs, not JSON size alone. Add optional model distribution, opted-in trial-user and licensed-user downloads, support and infrastructure floor to the existing economics ledger. Separate model-free installations from actual pack adoption rather than charging a model download to every install. Local inference has no baseline hosted-token charge. New limits, hosted retention allocations and commercial activation stay with their existing engineering and human gates.

## Packaging enterprise and offline operation

The ordinary desktop/analysis-console installer is lightweight by default and includes no mandatory model pack, model-specific runtime payload or inference residency. Core collection, deterministic findings, qualified local answers, history and export work without a model under surviving valid feature grants and their adopted offline policy. Purchased Local feature rights do not depend on an ongoing hosted connection or Local subscription; temporary subscription-covered access follows the separately adopted offline policy. An eligible user can choose to download a versioned signed local model pack containing the approved assets and required runtime dependencies, then enable or disable it. Pack installation is optional; the application must not auto-download it during first run or a normal update. Headless NAS/sensor/collector packages remain model-free.

Provide separate user-visible states for not installed, downloading, installed but disabled, enabled, incompatible and unavailable, with bounded progress/error details. Users can cancel a download, disable inference or remove the pack. Removal releases model-owned runtime/assets, caches and staged/rollback files under the existing package lifecycle while preserving shared application dependencies and local observation history. A subsequent app update must preserve the user’s model-free choice. Installed enabled packs infer entirely locally and work offline; air-gapped users may import an approved signed pack through the same trust checks.

Managed policy can pin, allowlist, disable and tighten the selected runtime/model profile. Precedence must be explicit and survive restart; policy may restrict optional use but does not silently opt a lightweight client into installation. No silent cloud calls on missing assets, denied GPU access, failed license checks or offline startup. Later customer-operated and air-gapped packages reuse the canonical contracts but require their own authentication, update, restore and parity qualification.

Use the existing trust/updater ownership for the optional model pack and its download/import/removal lifecycle. Validate signature, hash, source conversion/provenance, license notices, runtime/tokenizer/config compatibility and target profile before activation. Stage a complete candidate, atomically select it, retain only an eligible bounded known-good rollback, and recover from interruption or disk full. Reverify full, delta and resumed transfers. A revoked/incompatible or downgrade-disallowed bundle cannot be a rollback target. Offline imports perform the same checks without an online fallback; document how freshness/revocation knowledge is limited to the imported trusted policy. Uninstall removes owned assets according to the selected package policy without deleting independent customer exports.

### Approved product direction

- **Pillar Local:** $79 one-time purchase for the existing three-endpoint allowance. The desktop application and qualified optional Chromium companion use one Local license; a browser tab/extension is not a separate endpoint or purchase.
- **Full trial:** 30 days of full product use replace the permanent full-Free path for new offers. Trial expiry never revokes another valid purchased, subscription-derived or retained legacy grant. Without any surviving grant, new diagnostic use requires new valid coverage; retained reports/exports remain available. Existing data expiry and access controls still apply; preserved access is not a new indefinite-storage promise.
- **Acquired rights:** the purchase includes 12 months of feature updates. Features/versions received within the acquired rights remain usable perpetually without buying another update period. The Local license is not an always-on subscription.
- **Optional update renewal:** $29 buys a fresh 12 months of feature updates starting from the renewal purchase, with no automatic renewal by default. No backdated fees or charges for skipped years apply. Letting update eligibility lapse must not expire acquired Local feature rights.
- **Hosted services and temporary Local access:** History $19/month, Team $99/month, Fleet $399/month and the existing Enterprise recurring offer remain recurring. Active cloud/team coverage includes Local and companion use for the subscription’s covered endpoints without a separate $79 purchase; that access does not grant a perpetual Local license. When covered subscription access ends, retain saved reports/exports and every other valid Local or legacy grant; new diagnostic use requires a purchase only if no surviving grant covers it. No ads are introduced.
- **Optional model:** the signed model pack remains separately optional to install and enable, with local-only inference and useful model-free operation. Licensing never gives model prose a stronger evidence grade.

These are approved planning inputs. Record subscription-covered endpoint scope and the renewal purchase timestamp exactly in the versioned offer/receipt. Currency/tax/checkout disclosures, other unresolved entitlement details and security/support periods remain subject to the human release packet; this document does not choose missing terms.

### Narrow implementation boundary

Keep local feature entitlement separate from source consent, privacy grants, model installation, cloud subscription and evidence quality. The UI/API/MCP/controller dispatch layer admits an operation under the union of surviving valid trial, purchased Local, subscription-derived and retained legacy grants. Ending one grant never revokes another or forces a redundant purchase. The engine itself remains deterministic given the authorized inputs and versions; it must not raise or lower an evidence grade based on payment. Do not turn an expired trial into a fabricated current answer, an invented live alert or a green health state.

Represent Local access as a signed, versioned receipt that the application verifies locally against trusted public verification material. Distinguish purchased perpetual feature rights from temporary subscription access. Bind a purchased Local license’s existing three-endpoint allowance, or the subscription’s covered endpoint set, to existing endpoint identity semantics without counting the companion, a model pack or a rotated observation pseudonym as another endpoint. Store the receipt and licensing state through the existing durable local lifecycle. The exact issuance, import, endpoint replacement/recovery and anti-tamper policy must be specified by the existing entitlement tasks before shipping; none is silently approved here.

Separate three decisions in code: permission to use an acquired feature; eligibility to obtain a newly released feature/version; and trust/compatibility of the executable package. The end of an update window affects the second decision, not the first. Purchased acquired Local feature rights must continue through an Internet outage or an unavailable licensing/cloud service. Do not add a recurring lease renewal or always-online check that deactivates those rights. Temporary subscription access follows its signed coverage boundary and the explicitly adopted offline policy; a network error alone is not proof of cancellation or revocation. A genuinely invalid signature, incompatible package or absent grant is a distinct state from inability to contact a server.

Trial timing and receipt recovery require explicit, testable rules. Trial start, clock rollback, suspend/restart, offline exhaustion and pending purchase must not be improvised by the UI. A $29 update renewal starts a fresh 12 months from its purchase, even after a gap, with no backdating or skipped-year fees. Persist that effective purchase timestamp idempotently. When temporary cloud access ends, recompute every surviving valid grant, including legacy rights, without converting subscription-only features into perpetual ones. Do not erase reports, silently downgrade executable packages or remove separately purchased rights as part of that transition.

Keep report access/export and new diagnosis as separate operations. Trial expiry must preserve rendering completed retained reports and exporting allowed retained data without granting unrestricted new analysis through another entry point. It must not delete user evidence as a paywall. Display the last observed time, stopped/unavailable coverage and the reason new diagnosis is unavailable. All retained-data reads still honor authorization, consent and existing TTLs.

### Browser updates and security support

Enforce acquired feature/version eligibility with the signed entitlement and capability contract, not by freezing an old Chrome/Chromium extension binary. Browser-managed extension updates and native-host compatibility are a separate lifecycle concern. Test the supported updated companion against the entitled local engine/native protocol, hide/refuse newly unentitled capabilities explicitly and preserve supported acquired features. An extension update does not create another seat or revoke a perpetual Local license.

Perpetual feature rights do not, by themselves, define an unlimited security-fix, OS/browser compatibility or support commitment. The human release packet must state exact supported versions, security-fix/support periods and safe handling when a runtime can no longer operate securely. Do not promise indefinite patches, silently stop security fixes when the feature-update window ends, require an insecure old extension, or invent forced paid-upgrade terms. If compatibility cannot preserve an acquired feature on a supported profile, surface the conflict for an explicit decision rather than hiding it in licensing code.

### Open source and proprietary ownership boundary

Keep the core monorepo private. The intended publication boundary is component-level, not a blanket license for the repository:

- **Candidates for clean public extraction:** reviewed passive observation collectors, adapters/helpers, redaction/transport components, deliberately extracted public wire contracts, read-only SDK/sample integrations and synthetic fixtures.
